en.goal: Describe the position of furniture and objects using prepositions of place.

lessons.sofa-luminaria-em-cima: Sofa, lamp and on top of

phrases.t: The bed is next to the window.
phrases.scenario: You're describing your bedroom and where the bed is, next to the window. What do you say?

phrases.t: There is a lamp on the table.
phrases.scenario: Someone asks what's on the table — a lamp. What do you answer?

phrases.t: The cat is under the sofa.
phrases.scenario: You're looking for the cat and find it under the sofa. What do you say?

phrases.t: The blue chair is in front of the table.

sur-vs-dans.title: "Sur" or "dans"?
sur-vs-dans.body: Sur means "on top of", a surface: il y a une lampe sur la table. Dans means "inside", an enclosed space: il y a des vêtements dans l'armoire. The distinction is the same as English on vs. in.

review.pt: já que às vezes usamos "em" pras duas situações
review.en: The distinction is the same as English on vs. in.
review.why: Original PT note compared with Portuguese "em"; an English learner needs no such comparison. Replaced with an English-based remark (on/in map onto sur/dans here). Exceptions (on the wall, on the bus) deliberately omitted because not verified.
'sur' covers both 'on' and 'on top of'; PT gloss is only 'em cima de'.
